(* dy rmsn_b x: with y = x/r, (dy - y mean(y dy)) / r *)
rmsnRowsB[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](dy: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], x: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (n, d) = x.sizes
    rr = vec(n, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => SQRT ((SUM[j <- 0#d] (x[i,j])^2) / d + epsRms))
    y = mat(n, d, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => x[i,j] / rr[i])
    yd = vec(n, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => (SUM[j <- 0#d] y[i,j] dy[i,j]) / d)
    mat(n, d, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => (dy[i,j] - y[i,j] yd[i]) / rr[i])
  end
(* sm⍤1: softmax of each row *)
smRows[\nat r, nat c\](z: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (n, d) = z.sizes
    mx = vec(n, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => BIG MAX[j <- 0#d] z[i,j])
    e = mat(n, d, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => exp(z[i,j] - mx[i]))
    sums = vec(n, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => SUM[j <- 0#d] e[i,j])
    mat(n, d, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => e[i,j] / sums[i])
  end
(* p sm_b dy: p (dy - sum(p dy)) per row *)
smRowsB[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](pm: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], dy: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (n, d) = pm.sizes
    pd = vec(n, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => SUM[j <- 0#d] pm[i,j] dy[i,j])
    mat(n, d, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => pm[i,j] (dy[i,j] - pd[i]))
  end
(* tactic 9: the causal mask as an additive matrix, ¯1E10 above the diagonal *)
causalMask: Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    mat(blockSize, blockSize, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => if j > i then -(10.0^10) else 0.0 end)

(* --------------------------------------------------- the loaders -------- *)
(* decimal digits, optional '.', optional e/E exponent; leading '-' or '¯' *)
parseFloat(s: String): RR64 = do
    neg = (s[0] = '-') OR (s[0] = '¯')
    m: RR64 := 0.0
    scale: ZZ32 := 0
    ex: ZZ32 := 0
    i: ZZ32 := if neg then 1 else 0 end
    seenPoint: Boolean := false
    n = |s|
    while (i < n) AND: ((s[i] =/= 'e') AND (s[i] =/= 'E')) do
        c = s[i]
        if c = '.' then seenPoint := true
        else
            m := 10.0 m + (c.codePoint - '0'.codePoint)
            if seenPoint then scale += 1 end
        end
        i += 1
    end
    if i < n then
        eneg = (s[i+1] = '-') OR (s[i+1] = '¯')
        j = if eneg OR (s[i+1] = '+') then i + 2 else i + 1 end
        ex := strToInt(s[j # (n - j)])
        if eneg then ex := -ex end
    end
    e10 = ex - scale
    r = if e10 >= 0 then m (10.0^e10)
        elif e10 >= -22 then m / (10.0^(-e10))
        else (m / (10.0^22)) / (10.0^(-e10 - 22)) end
    if neg then -r else r end
  end
(* every space-separated number on a line goes to out[off..]; returns the count *)
parseRow[\nat s\](line: String, out: Vector[\RR64,s\], off: ZZ32): ZZ32 = do
    n = |line|
    i: ZZ32 := 0
    k: ZZ32 := 0
    while i < n do
        if line[i] = ' ' then i += 1
        else
            j: ZZ32 := i
            while (j < n) AND: (line[j] =/= ' ') do j += 1 end
            out[off + k] := parseFloat(line[i # (j - i)])
            k += 1
            i := j
        end
    end
    k
  end

    for i <- seq(0#9) do

docLength(d: ZZ32): ZZ32 = corpusLengths[d]
tokenAt(d: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): ZZ32 = corpusTokens[d, j]

(* ------------------------- the step: keys -> (loss, flat gradient). Pure. -- *)
step(p: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], b: Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\]): (RR64, Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]) = do
    bsz = |b|
    n = bsz blockSize
    ids = keys(n, fn (r: ZZ32): ZZ32 => corpusTokens[b[r DIV blockSize], r MOD blockSize])
    tg = keys(n, fn (r: ZZ32): ZZ32 => corpusTokens[b[r DIV blockSize], (r MOD blockSize) + 1])
    vm = vec(n, fn (r: ZZ32): RR64 => if (r MOD blockSize) < corpusLengths[b[r DIV blockSize]] then 1.0 else 0.0 end)
    nv = SUM[r <- 0#n] vm[r]
    pos = keys(n, fn (r: ZZ32): ZZ32 => r MOD blockSize)
    wte = view(p, 0); wpe = view(p, 1); lm = view(p, 2)
    wq = view(p, 3); wk = view(p, 4); wv = view(p, 5); wo = view(p, 6)
    f1 = view(p, 7); f2 = view(p, 8)
    (* -- forward, all (doc,pos) rows at once -- *)
    x = gather(wte, ids) + gather(wpe, pos)
    xp = rmsnRows(x); x1 = rmsnRows(xp)
    q = x1 (wq^T); kk = x1 (wk^T); vv = x1 (wv^T)
    att = zerosM(bsz nHead blockSize, blockSize)
    hc = zerosM(n, nEmbd)
    for d <- 0#bsz, h <- 0#nHead do
        qh = head(q, d, h); kh = head(kk, d, h); vh = head(vv, d, h)
        ah = headCell(att, d, h)
        assignInto(ah, smRows((qh (kh^T)) / (SQRT (1.0 headDim)) + causalMask))
        assignInto(head(hc, d, h), ah vh)
    end
    x2 = xp + hc (wo^T)
    x3 = rmsnRows(x2); m0 = x3 (f1^T); mr = relu(m0)
    x4 = x2 + mr (f2^T)
    pr = smRows(x4 (lm^T))
    loss = -(SUM[r <- 0#n] vm[r] (log(pr[r, tg[r]]))) / nv
    (* -- backward, one line under each forward line, bottom-up -- *)
    g = zeros(nParams())
    dL = scaleRows(vm / nv, pr - onehot(tg, vocabSize))
    assignInto(view(g, 2), (dL^T) x4); dX4 = dL lm
    assignInto(view(g, 8), (dX4^T) mr); dM0 = hadamard(dX4 f2, positive(m0))
    assignInto(view(g, 7), (dM0^T) x3); dX3 = dM0 f1
    dX2 = dX4 + rmsnRowsB(dX3, x2)
    assignInto(view(g, 6), (dX2^T) hc); dH = dX2 wo

       and m.put((i,j),x) -- so APL's indexed and selective assignment are
       in-place puts.  That is what lets an APL variable be a plain lambda
       parameter: the name never has to be rebound (apl gap row 29 says it
       cannot be) and nothing is copied.
   (b) the library's own row view m[1,:] is NOT an AnyVector (merged ledger
       row 54, re-confirmed here over a runtime-sized matrix), so it carries no
       vector algebra; but a 6-line user object extending Vector (row 55) is one,
       and its nat parameters are inferred from the runtime-built matrix.  So
       m[1;] and m[;1] are zero-copy views with the full algebra.

       vector index are an excluding pair and the rank of an indexed result is

    put(ij:(ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i,j) = ij; base.put((r0 + i, c0 + j), x) end
    init0(ij:(ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i,j) = ij; base.init0((r0 + i, c0 + j), x) end
    replica[\U\](): Array2[\U,0,r,0,c\] = array2[\U,r,c\]()
end
blockOf[\nat br, nat bc, nat r, nat c\](base: Matrix[\RR64,br,bc\], r0: ZZ32, c0: ZZ32, _: N[\r\], _: N[\c\]): Matrix[\RR64,r,c\] =
    Block[\br,bc,r,c\](base, r0, c0)
block[\nat br, nat bc\](base: Matrix[\RR64,br,bc\], r0: ZZ32, c0: ZZ32, rows: ZZ32, cols: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    blockOf(base, r0, c0, reflect(rows), reflect(cols))
head[\nat br, nat bc\](a: Matrix[\RR64,br,bc\], d: ZZ32, h: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    block(a, d blockSize, h headDim, blockSize, headDim)
headCell[\nat br, nat bc\](a: Matrix[\RR64,br,bc\], d: ZZ32, h: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    block(a, (d nHead + h) blockSize, 0, blockSize, blockSize)
assignInto[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](dest: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], src: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]): () = do
    dest.assign(fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => src[i,j])
  end

opr (m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\])^T[\nat r, nat c\]: Matrix[\RR64,c,r\] = m.t()
opr /[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], s: RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    mat(rows, cols, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => m[i,j] / s)
  end

smRows[\nat r, nat c\](z: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (n, d) = z.sizes
    mx = vec(n, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => BIG MAX[j <- 0#d] z[i,j])
    e = mat(n, d, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => exp(z[i,j] - mx[i]))
    sums = vec(n, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => SUM[j <- 0#d] e[i,j])
    mat(n, d, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => e[i,j] / sums[i])
  end
smRowsB[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](pm: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], dy: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (n, d) = pm.sizes
    pd = vec(n, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => SUM[j <- 0#d] pm[i,j] dy[i,j])
    mat(n, d, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => pm[i,j] (dy[i,j] - pd[i]))
  end
causalMask: Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    mat(blockSize, blockSize, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => if j > i then -(10.0^10) else 0.0 end)

(* -------------------------------------------------------- test data ----- *)
q: Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = mat(nn, nEmbd, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => sin(0.1 i + 0.37 j))
kk: Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = mat(nn, nEmbd, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => sin(0.1 i + 0.37 j + 1.0))
vv: Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = mat(nn, nEmbd, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => sin(0.1 i + 0.37 j + 2.0))
dH: Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = mat(nn, nEmbd, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => sin(0.1 i + 0.37 j + 3.0))

sumOf[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): RR64 = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    SUM[i <- 0#rows, j <- 0#cols] m[i,j]
  end

(* ------------------------------------------------ form A: the attention -- *)
attnA(): (Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\], Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\], Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\],
          Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\], Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\], Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]) = do
    att = zerosM(bsz nHead blockSize, blockSize)
    hc = zerosM(nn, nEmbd)
    for d <- 0#bsz, h <- 0#nHead do
        qh = head(q, d, h); kh = head(kk, d, h); vh = head(vv, d, h)
        ah = headCell(att, d, h)
        assignInto(ah, smRows((qh (kh^T)) / (SQRT (1.0 headDim)) + causalMask))
        assignInto(head(hc, d, h), ah vh)
    end
    dQ = zerosM(nn, nEmbd); dK = zerosM(nn, nEmbd); dV = zerosM(nn, nEmbd)
    dSa = zerosM(bsz nHead blockSize, blockSize)
    for d <- 0#bsz, h <- 0#nHead do
        ah = headCell(att, d, h); dh = head(dH, d, h)
        qh = head(q, d, h); kh = head(kk, d, h); vh = head(vv, d, h)
        assignInto(head(dV, d, h), (ah^T) dh)
        dS = smRowsB(ah, dh (vh^T)) / (SQRT (1.0 headDim))
        assignInto(headCell(dSa, d, h), dS)
        assignInto(head(dQ, d, h), dS kh)
        assignInto(head(dK, d, h), (dS^T) qh)
    end
    (att, hc, dSa, dQ, dK, dV)
  end

report(att: Matrix[\RR64,a1,a2\], hc: Matrix[\RR64,b1,b2\], dSa: Matrix[\RR64,c1,c2\],
       dQ: Matrix[\RR64,d1,d2\], dK: Matrix[\RR64,e1,e2\], dV: Matrix[\RR64,f1,f2\])
      [\nat a1, nat a2, nat b1, nat b2, nat c1, nat c2, nat d1, nat d2, nat e1, nat e2, nat f1, nat f2\]: () = do
    println "att sum " sumOf(att)
    println "dS  sum " sumOf(dSa)
    println "hc  sum " sumOf(hc) "  hc[5,7] " hc[5,7]
    println "dQ  sum " sumOf(dQ) "  dQ[5,7] " dQ[5,7]
    println "dK  sum " sumOf(dK) "  dK[5,7] " dK[5,7]
    println "dV  sum " sumOf(dV) "  dV[5,7] " dV[5,7]
  end

run(): () = do
    (att, hc, dSa, dQ, dK, dV) = attnA()
    report(att, hc, dSa, dQ, dK, dV)
    t0 = nanoTime()
    for r <- seq(0#10) do
        (a2, h2, s2, q2, k2, v2) = attnA()
    end
    println "form A: 10 reps of forward+backward " ((nanoTime() - t0) DIV 1000000) " ms"
  end
end

head = '''(* att_b -- run-c3 attention probe, form B: a `cells` lift over a uniform
   layout.  Every per-head array is a matrix of N rows whose columns are the
   NH heads side by side; cell (d,h) of a matrix with c columns is the
   zero-copy block(m, 16 d, h (c DIV 4), 16, c DIV 4).  No array is copied. *)
component att_b
export Executable
import NatReflect.{...}
import System.{...}

'''
tail = '''(* -------------------------------------------------------- test data ----- *)
q: Array[\\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\\] = mat(nn, nEmbd, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => sin(0.1 i + 0.37 j))
k: Array[\\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\\] = mat(nn, nEmbd, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => sin(0.1 i + 0.37 j + 1.0))
v: Array[\\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\\] = mat(nn, nEmbd, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => sin(0.1 i + 0.37 j + 2.0))
dH: Array[\\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\\] = mat(nn, nEmbd, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => sin(0.1 i + 0.37 j + 3.0))

sumOf[\\nat r, nat c\\](m: Matrix[\\RR64,r,c\\]): RR64 = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    SUM[i <- 0#rows, j <- 0#cols] m[i,j]
  end

(* ------------------------------------------------------ the cells lift -- *)
(* typed readers on a cell result, AplCore's assemble-by-first-result *)
colsOfA[\\nat r, nat c\\](m: Matrix[\\RR64,r,c\\]): ZZ32 = do (rows, cols) = m.sizes; cols end
nth2[\\nat r, nat c\\](m: Matrix[\\RR64,r,c\\], i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 = m[i,j]

cell[\\nat r, nat c\\](m: Matrix[\\RR64,r,c\\], d: ZZ32, h: ZZ32): Array[\\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\\] = do
    (rows, cols) = m.sizes
    w = cols DIV nHead
    block(m, d blockSize, h w, blockSize, w)
  end

typedef Cell = Array[\\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\\]

cells(f: (Cell, Cell) -> Cell, a: Cell, b: Cell): Array[\\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\\] = do
    rs = array[\\Any\\](bsz nHead)
    for d <- 0#bsz, h <- 0#nHead do rs[d nHead + h] := f(cell(a,d,h), cell(b,d,h)) end
    w = colsOfA(rs[0])
    mat(nn, nHead w, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 =>
        nth2(rs[(i DIV blockSize) nHead + (j DIV w)], i MOD blockSize, j MOD w))
  end

cells(f: (Cell, Cell, Cell) -> Cell, a: Cell, b: Cell, c: Cell): Array[\\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\\] = do
    rs = array[\\Any\\](bsz nHead)
    for d <- 0#bsz, h <- 0#nHead do rs[d nHead + h] := f(cell(a,d,h), cell(b,d,h), cell(c,d,h)) end
    w = colsOfA(rs[0])
    mat(nn, nHead w, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 =>
        nth2(rs[(i DIV blockSize) nHead + (j DIV w)], i MOD blockSize, j MOD w))
  end

(* the same lift, writing through block views into a preallocated matrix; the
   width still has to come from a first result, so it is two lines longer *)
cellsW(f: (Cell, Cell) -> Cell, a: Cell, b: Cell): Array[\\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\\] = do
    w = colsOfA(f(cell(a,0,0), cell(b,0,0)))
    out = zerosM(nn, nHead w)
    for d <- 0#bsz, h <- 0#nHead do assignInto(cell(out,d,h), f(cell(a,d,h), cell(b,d,h))) end
    out
  end

(* named top-level cell functions, the alternative to the lambdas *)
scores(qc: Cell, kc: Cell): Cell = smRows((qc (kc^T)) / (SQRT (1.0 headDim)) + causalMask)
weigh(ac: Cell, vc: Cell): Cell = ac vc
backV(ac: Cell, dc: Cell): Cell = (ac^T) dc
backS(ac: Cell, dc: Cell, vc: Cell): Cell = smRowsB(ac, dc (vc^T))
backQ(sc: Cell, kc: Cell): Cell = sc kc
backK(sc: Cell, qc: Cell): Cell = (sc^T) qc

(* ---------------------------------------------- form B: the attention --- *)
attnB(): (Cell, Cell, Cell, Cell, Cell, Cell) = do
    att = cells(fn (qc: Cell, kc: Cell): Cell => smRows((qc (kc^T)) / (SQRT (1.0 headDim)) + causalMask), q, k)
    hc  = cells(fn (ac: Cell, vc: Cell): Cell => ac vc, att, v)
    dV  = cells(fn (ac: Cell, dc: Cell): Cell => (ac^T) dc, att, dH)
    dS  = cells(fn (ac: Cell, dc: Cell): Cell => smRowsB(ac, dc), att,
                cells(fn (dc: Cell, vc: Cell): Cell => dc (vc^T), dH, v)) / (SQRT (1.0 headDim))
    dQ  = cells(fn (sc: Cell, kc: Cell): Cell => sc kc, dS, k)
    dK  = cells(fn (sc: Cell, qc: Cell): Cell => (sc^T) qc, dS, q)
    (att, hc, dS, dQ, dK, dV)
  end

(* the same six lines with the three-argument lift and the named functions *)
attnB3(): (Cell, Cell, Cell, Cell, Cell, Cell) = do
    att = cells(scores, q, k)
    hc  = cells(weigh, att, v)
    dV  = cells(backV, att, dH)
    dS  = cells(backS, att, dH, v) / (SQRT (1.0 headDim))
    dQ  = cells(backQ, dS, k)
    dK  = cells(backK, dS, q)
    (att, hc, dS, dQ, dK, dV)
  end

(* the write-through variant of the forward, for the copy comparison *)
attnBW(): (Cell, Cell) = do
    att = cellsW(scores, q, k)
    hc  = cellsW(weigh, att, v)
    (att, hc)
  end

report(att: Cell, hc: Cell, dSa: Cell, dQ: Cell, dK: Cell, dV: Cell): () = do
    println "att sum " sumOf(att)
    println "dS  sum " sumOf(dSa)
    println "hc  sum " sumOf(hc) "  hc[5,7] " hc[5,7]
    println "dQ  sum " sumOf(dQ) "  dQ[5,7] " dQ[5,7]
    println "dK  sum " sumOf(dK) "  dK[5,7] " dK[5,7]
    println "dV  sum " sumOf(dV) "  dV[5,7] " dV[5,7]
  end

run(): () = do
    (att, hc, dSa, dQ, dK, dV) = attnB()
    report(att, hc, dSa, dQ, dK, dV)
    println "-- three-argument lift + named functions --"
    (a3, h3, s3, q3, k3, v3) = attnB3()
    report(a3, h3, s3, q3, k3, v3)
    println "-- write-through cellsW, forward only --"
    (aw, hw) = attnBW()
    println "att sum " sumOf(aw) "  hc  sum " sumOf(hw) "  hc[5,7] " hw[5,7]
    t0 = nanoTime()
    for r <- seq(0#10) do
        (a2, h2, s2, q2, k2, v2) = attnB()
    end
    println "form B: 10 reps of forward+backward " ((nanoTime() - t0) DIV 1000000) " ms"
  end
end
'''

This directory contains Emacs commands for converting Fortress code into LaTeX
commands for the purposes of formatting. In order for LaTeX to understand the
formatted code, you need to import the fortify.sty package in your LaTeX file:

\usepackage{$FORTRESS_HOME/Fortify/fortify.sty}

Emacs Formatting Commands
-------------------------
The main command "fortify", also bound to the key M-& (meta-ampersand).
formats a portion of the text in the buffer as Fortress code by inserting TeX
commands and performing certain transformations, which include replacing all-caps
identifiers with appropriate mathematical symbols.

With no prefix argument, the contiguous nonblank text preceding point is formatted.
Here are some examples.  In each case assume that I have typed the text on the left
and then hit M-& (in fact,  this is exactly what I am about to do to create the
examples!); the replacement text is shown on the right.

	x		\VAR{x}
	foo		\VAR{foo}
	GCD		\OPR{GCD}
	Thread		\TYP{Thread}
	spawn		\KWD{spawn}
	UNION		\EXP{\cup}
	a+b		\EXP{a+b}
	foo+bar		\EXP{\VAR{foo}+\VAR{bar}}

The formatting relies on TeX macros called \VAR, \OPR, \KWD, \TYP, and \EXP:

	\VAR		variables
	\OPR		identifiers used as operators
	\KWD		keywords
	\TYP		types
	\EXP		general expressions

In general, each formats its argument in math mode, but with some extra
processing: \VAR applies \mathit, \OPR and \KWD apply \mathtt, and \TYP applies
\mathrm; \OPR uses \mathbin spacing and \KWD uses \mathrel spacing (but
sometimes extra fixup formatting is inserted within an \EXP to handle situations
not covered well by TeX's math spacing rules); and all of them add a little
extra \mathsurround space, the effect of which is to set these expressions off a
little bit when they are used in running text.  This extra space shows up before
commas and periods, too, which is intentional, so you can easily tell that the
sentence punctuation is not part of the expression.

(Through a bit of internal chicanery, \VAR and \OPR and \KWD and \TYP
do not provide the extra \mathsurround space when they are used within
a larger Fortress-formatting context such as the argument to \EXP.
Uses of \EXP should not be nested.)

What if you want to format an expression that contains whitespace?
Use a C-U prefix, and M-& will format the region instead.  So, when
you are just typing merrily along, if you foresee typing an expression
containing spaces, just hit C-Space at the beginning of the expression
to set the mark, then type the expression, then type C-U M-& to
format the expression, then keep on typing.  Here are some examples:

	a UNION b	    \EXP{a \cup b}
	do x+=1; x end	    \EXP{\KWD{do}\:x\mathrel{+}=1; x \KWD{end}}
	{ a^2 | a<-1:10 }   \EXP{\{\,a^{2} \mid a\leftarrow{}1\COLONOP{}10\,\}}
	<\a,b,c,d\>         \EXP{\langle{}a,b,c,d\rangle}
	<\ a,b,c,d \>       \EXP{\langle\,a,b,c,d\,\rangle}

Note the use of \mathrel in second example to correct a spacing problem.  Note
also the insertion of thin spaces within the braces in the third example; in
general, the formatting process tries to honor the use of whitespace in the raw
ASCII form, and the presence or absence of whitespace inside enclosing operators is
reflected in the formatting by the presence or absence of a TeX thin space.  To see

cd /home/user/fortress/explorations/run-c3/probes && cat > att_REPORT.md <<'MDEOF'
# run-c3 probe: three shapes for microGPT's attention

Files: `att_a.fss` (form A, round one's block-view loops), `att_b.fss`
(form B, a `cells` lift over a uniform zero-copy layout), `att_c.fss`
(form C, per-head cells as values in a rank-3 array), plus
`att_b_untyped.fss` (the untyped-lambda question on its own).
Outputs `att_*.out` (= the one-thread run), `att_*.t1.out`, `att_*.t4.out`;
renders `att_*.tic` / `att_*.svg` / `att_*.png`.

Test data: B = 2 documents, N = 32, `nEmbd` 16, `blockSize` 16, `nHead` 4,
`headDim` 4; `q`, `k`, `v`, `dH` are 32x16 with `sin(0.1 i + 0.37 j + c)`,
c = 0, 1, 2, 3; the mask is round one's additive `-1E10` above the diagonal.
Environment: `experiment/env.sh` (JDK 25, `-Xmx4g`), walk interpreter.

## The three forms

| | A `att_a.fss` | B `att_b.fss` | C `att_c.fss` |
|---|---|---|---|
| shape | `for d, h` over `head`/`headCell` block views, `assignInto` | `cells(f, a, b)` over a uniform N-row layout, cells are `block(m, 16d, h (c DIV 4), 16, c DIV 4)` | `heads`/`unheads` copies into `Array3`, `cells(f, s, t)` over `Plane` views |
| `att` layout | (B·NH·16) x 16 stacked | N x 64 (head cells side by side) | rank 3, (B·NH) x 16 x 16 |
| block lines (fwd+bwd) | **17** (19 in the probe: two extra lines only to expose `dS` for the checksum) | **6** logical / 7 physical | **7** logical / 8 physical |
| helper lines beyond the shared header | **0** | **14** (`colsOfA` 1, `nth2` 1, `cell` 5, `cells` 7); +7 for the three-argument overload, +6 for `cellsW` | **34** (`arr3` 1, `Plane` 7, `plane` 1, `rowsOfA`/`colsOfA`/`nth2` 3, `heads` 6, `unheads` 5, `cells` 7, rank-3 `opr /` 4) |
| copied in | nothing — `q k v dH att` are read through `Block` views | nothing — same `Block` views, one `cell` function for all widths | **4 x 512 = 2048 floats** (`heads` of `q k v dH`) |
| copied out | nothing — `unheads` has no counterpart | nothing | **4 x 512 = 2048 floats** (`unheads` of `hc dV dQ dK`) |
| assembled / written | `assignInto` writes 4096 floats into 5 preallocated matrices (att 2048, hc/dV/dQ/dK 512 each); per-cell temporaries a further 6144 | seven `mat` fills, 8192 floats, plus 2048 for the `/ SQRT` of `dS` = **10240**; no per-cell temporaries survive | same 10240 as B, in `Array3`, **plus the 4096 of relayout** |
| t1, 10 reps fwd+bwd | **12994 ms** (5 passes: 12345–13454) | **13889 ms** (13600–14523) | **15664 ms** (15243–16128) |
| t4, 10 reps fwd+bwd | **5361 ms** (5361–10260) | **6319 ms** (5457–8145) | **7746 ms** (6702–12183) |

Net float traffic is the same for A and B — A's per-cell temporaries
(`dh (vh^T)`, `smRowsB`, the scaling) are exactly the arrays B names at
N-row scale, 6144 floats either way. Form C is the only form that copies:
4096 floats of pure layout shuffling, +40% on the traffic, +21% on the clock.

### Checksums — identical across all three forms and both thread counts

```
att sum 128.0
dS  sum 1.5144135945277526E-15
hc  sum -7.426586484624076  hc[5,7] -0.980921927237238
dQ  sum 0.7870326833403783  dQ[5,7] -0.015176485293592131
dK  sum -1.2490009027033011E-15  dK[5,7] 0.008389135263650555
dV  sum 16.951785001661463  dV[5,7] 0.22233390744644332
```

Every digit agrees: `att_a.t1.out`, `att_b.t1.out`, `att_c.t1.out` and the
three `.t4.out` files differ only in the timing lines (`diff` of the
non-timing lines is empty in all six pairings). So the four-thread results
equal the one-thread results for all three forms, and the three forms agree
entry by entry — round one's ledger row 155 re-confirmed for two further
parallel shapes (a parallel `for` filling an `Array[\Any\]` of cell results,
and a parallel `for` over planes).

`dS sum` and `dK sum` are structurally ~0 (softmax backward sums to zero per
row); the fixed entries `dK[5,7]` and `dQ[5,7]` carry the discrimination.

### How each forward reads in the render

- **A** (`att_a.png`): six lines of scaffolding around two of arithmetic —
  the `for`, three view bindings, `ah`, then `assignInto(ah, smRows(...))`
  and `assignInto(head(hc, d, h), ah vh)`. The transpose and `√headDim`
  render, but the two matrix expressions are buried inside `assignInto(...)`
  and the loop indices `d, h` appear eleven times.
- **B** (`att_b.png`): two clean equations, `att = cells(fn (qc, kc) ⇒
  smRows((qc (kc^T))/(√1.0 headDim) + causalMask), q, k)` and
  `hc = cells(fn (ac, vc) ⇒ ac vc, att, v)` — the Dyalog's two forward
  lines, one Fortress line each, with the rank operator spelled `cells`
  and the cell function in-line. No index appears at all.
- **C** (`att_c.png`): B's two lines plus the `h¨` line
  `(qh, kh, vh, dHh) = (heads(q), heads(k), heads(v), heads(dH))` and a
  `unheads(...)` wrapper on every line that has to return to the N x 16
  layout — visually the closest to the Dyalog, textually the noisiest.

All six lines of every form rendered; nothing fell back to ASCII.

## Findings on the spellings the brief asked about

**1. Untyped lambda parameters WORK.** `att_b_untyped.fss` runs
`att = cells(fn (qc, kc) => smRows((qc (kc^T)) / (SQRT (1.0 headDim)) +
causalMask), q, k)` and prints `att sum 128.0`. The parameter types come
from the declared arrow type of `cells`'s `f`. `att_b.fss` therefore uses
untyped lambdas throughout, which is what makes its six lines read like the
Dyalog. (Typed lambdas — `fn (qc: Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\], kc:
Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] => ...` — also work,
and were what the first working version used; they are simply unreadable.)

**2. A type alias for the cell type does NOT work.** This is the reason the
untyped lambda matters so much: the typed spelling cannot be abbreviated.

- `type Cell = Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]` →
  `** bug! Not yet implemented: TypeAlias at /home/user/fortress/explorations/run-c3/probes/att_b.fss:91.1`
  (the walk interpreter aborts the whole component).
- `typedef Cell = Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]` → `Cell is undefined.`, once
  per use (`typedef` is not a Fortress keyword; the grammar has
  `TypeAlias ::= type Id StaticParams? = TypeRef`,
  `Specification/appendices/grammars/concrete-syntax.tex:425`).

So the declared type of a cell function must be written out in full at every
occurrence: `cells(f: (Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\], Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\])
-> Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\], a: Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\], b:
Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]` is one 178-character
line. This is a new gap-ledger candidate (not in
`fortress-gap-ledger.md`).

**3. The three-argument lift WORKS, overloaded on arity.** A second
`cells(f, a, b, c)` declared in the same component alongside the
two-argument one resolves correctly, and `dS = cells(backS, att, dH, v) /
(SQRT (1.0 headDim))` with `backS(ac, dc, vc) = smRowsB(ac, dc (vc^T))` is
one line instead of two. `att_b.t1.out`'s second checksum block is that
version and matches to the last digit.

**4. Named top-level cell functions WORK as arguments.** `att =
cells(scores, q, k)` with `scores(qc, kc): ... = smRows(...)` type-checks
and runs (`attnB3` in `att_b.fss`). They read *better* than the lambdas for
the backward lines — `dQ = cells(backQ, dS, k)` — and *worse* for the
forward, because the reader must jump to `scores` to see the Dyalog line.
The named version is also the only one that can take the three-argument
lift without an unreadable in-line lambda; the two mix cleanly.

**5. `cells` by fill beats `cellsW` by write-through.** The write-through
variant is one line shorter (6 against 7) but has to call `f` once on cell
(0,0) just to learn the result width before it can allocate, so it does 9
cell evaluations per call instead of 8. Measured on the forward alone,
10 reps: 5584 ms (`cells`) against 6318 ms (`cellsW`) at one thread,
2418 against 2869 at four — 13–19% slower, i.e. exactly the redundant
cell. Keep the fill. (Both are in `att_b.fss`; `cellsW`'s output is the
third checksum block and agrees.)

**6. Two declaration errors met on the way, both worth the ledger.**

- Static parameters may not follow the value parameters of an ordinary
  function. `report(att: Matrix[\RR64,a1,a2\], ...)[\nat a1, nat a2, ...\]:
  () = do` gives a bare `Syntax Error` at the declaration's own column
  (`att_a.fss:105:7`, with `null` printed before it). Only the postfix
  `opr` form takes them there (ledger row 149). The fix used here is to
  declare such a reporting function over the runtime type
  `Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]` instead of a `nat`-generic `Matrix`.
- A top-level value may not share a name with a `nat` static parameter of
  any generic function in the component. With `q: Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]`
  at top level, `assignInto[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\]` and
  `smRowsB[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\]` (round one's spellings) both fail
  with `Variable q is already declared.` at the static-parameter list
  (`att_a.fss:42:38`, `att_a.fss:59:35`). Renaming the static parameter
  (`nat s`) is the fix; renaming the data would have cost the Dyalog
  correspondence. This is ledger row 147's rule reaching in the other
  direction — the *static* parameter is what collides, and the collision is
  reported at the generic, not at the value.

## Recommendation

Take form B: at six lines it is the only form that puts one Fortress line
against one Dyalog line, it copies not one float more than round one's
loops, and it costs 7% over form A at one thread and scales the same at
four — a price worth paying to delete seventeen lines of index arithmetic
from the middle of the program. Write its cell functions as untyped lambdas
for the two forward lines and as named top-level functions for the
backward, declare both the two- and three-argument `cells`, and assemble by
`mat` fill rather than by write-through. Form C buys nothing: it is the
same six lines wrapped in `heads`/`unheads`, needs 34 lines of rank-3
machinery instead of 14, copies 4096 floats per step for layout alone, and
runs 21% slower — the `Array3` value is only worth it if a later stage
genuinely wants per-head arrays as values rather than as views.

| | A `att_a.fss` (round one) | B `att_b.fss` (`cells` lift, zero copy) | C `att_c.fss` (rank-3 with copies) |

| render | two matrix expressions buried inside `assignInto(...)`, `d, h` eleven times | two clean equations, one per Dyalog line, no index anywhere | B's lines plus the `h¨` line and a `unheads(...)` on every result — closest to the Dyalog, noisiest |
| | index arithmetic in the middle of the program, but nothing copied and nothing to explain | the Dyalog line for line, at 7% over A and identical copying | the Dyalog's own shape, paid for with 20 extra helper lines, 4096 floats and 21% |

Take form B: at six lines it is the only form that puts one Fortress line against one Dyalog line, it copies not one float more than round one's loops, and it costs 7% over A at one thread while scaling the same at four — worth it to delete seventeen lines of index arithmetic from the middle of the program. Write the forward cell functions as untyped lambdas and the backward ones as named top-level functions, declare both the two- and three-argument `cells`, and assemble by `mat` fill. Form C buys nothing the views do not already give: the same six lines wrapped in `heads`/`unheads`, 34 helper lines instead of 14, 4096 floats of relayout per step and 21% more time — worth revisiting only if a later stage wants per-head arrays as values rather than as views.
